plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets in the Southern Hemisphere spring turn lavender-blue as this tree opens its clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers. When the blooms fall, they cover pavements and lawns in a violet carpet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in the Southern Hemisphere, roughly October to November, with peak bloom in early to mid November in many places
plants.location: Pretoria, South Africa, and eastern Australia, including Brisbane and Sydney
plants.funFact: Jacaranda is native to South America, but it is now so closely tied to spring in Pretoria and Sydney that many locals treat its bloom as a seasonal marker. In Australian folklore, it is said to signal the start of exam season.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub opens delicate, lightly scented flowers while most gardens are fading. Its single or semi-double blooms have golden stamens at the center, and they brighten cool autumn days.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter, roughly October to December
plants.location: Southern Japan, and gardens in the southeastern United States
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, the tea plant, is a close relative of the sasanqua. The seeds of C. sasanqua are pressed to make a culinary and cosmetic oil in parts of Asia.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: Garden chrysanthemums bring autumn color in a wide range of shapes, from tidy buttons to shaggy spiders. They keep flowering through the first cool nights, and the blooms are often still going strong after other flowers have faded.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn, peaking from October into November
plants.location: Gardens and festivals across Japan, and temperate gardens in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are short-day plants. They set buds only when nights grow long enough, which is why they bloom in autumn.
